scopeNote: Recognition, acute treatment, electrical storm, idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias, inherited syndromes and ICD selection. Counts remain provisional pending coverage audit.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmia guideline 2022 and AHA ALS 2025
checked: Sustained VT duration or earlier hemodynamic intervention; AV dissociation and capture support ventricular origin without using absent signs to exclude VT.

sourceChecks.source: ESC SVT 2019 wide-complex differential; ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; AHA ALS 2025
checked: Brugada sequence: absence of RS in all precordial leads and RS interval when present; lack of visible dissociation does not exclude VT. Torsades requires long QT outside VT; sustained polymorphic VT unsynchronized shock and magnesium distinction from normal-QT polymorphic VT.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; digoxin US label 2025
checked: Bidirectional VT differential and digoxin toxicity context; life-threatening ventricular arrhythmia warrants Fab. Recent syncope suspicious for cardiac origin changes incidental NSVT urgency; initial ECG, echo and rhythm characterization with substrate-directed testing.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death guideline 2022
checked: Atypical ventricular-arrhythmia presentation warrants considering CMR despite a normal echo. Unexplained arrest requires systematic work-up; repeat QT and ventricular-function assessment after recovery, phenotype-directed testing and cautious genetic interpretation before idiopathic VF diagnosis.

sourceChecks.source: AHA 2025 cardiac arrest and tachyarrhythmia algorithms
checked: Pulseless VT defibrillation and immediate CPR; AHA shockable-pathway drug sequencing and doses. Monomorphic VT with attributable instability: synchronized cardioversion; avoid delay if synchronization impossible during critical deterioration.

sourceChecks.source: AHA ALS and tachyarrhythmia algorithm 2025; ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022
checked: Sustained polymorphic VT requires immediate unsynchronized shock. Selected tolerated monomorphic VT drug options and procainamide infusion stopping limits; unstable or drug-ineligible patients require electrical strategy.

sourceChecks.source: PROCAMIO primary trial; AHA 2025 tachyarrhythmia algorithm
checked: PROCAMIO selected tolerated population, 62 main-analysis patients, trial regimens and 40-minute safety/termination outcomes. Independent procainamide stop criteria; QRS change 150 to 235 ms exceeds fifty percent despite cumulative dose below maximum.

sourceChecks.source: AHA 2025 algorithms; EHRA antiarrhythmic clinical-use consensus
checked: Perfusing-rhythm amiodarone load distinguished from arrest bolus and lidocaine arrest doses. Magnesium for long-QT torsades despite normal serum magnesium, removal of trigger, potassium correction and evidence limitation around exact high-normal target.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022 and AHA ALS 2025
checked: Refractory acquired long-QT torsades: rate acceleration after trigger correction and magnesium; distinguish congenital and ischemic exceptions. Normal-QT polymorphic VT with active ischemia: coronary treatment and selected lidocaine/amiodarone, not routine magnesium or isoproterenol.

sourceChecks.source: EHRA multisociety electrical storm consensus 2024
checked: At least three sustained ventricular episodes within 24 hours separated by at least five minutes requiring intervention; ATP qualifies and multiple shocks need episode verification. Parallel stabilization, device interrogation, sympathetic distress treatment and reversible-trigger search.

sourceChecks.source: EHRA storm consensus 2024; propranolol/metoprolol primary randomized trial 2018
checked: Nonselective beta blockade with IV amiodarone in eligible structural-heart-disease storm; trial doses distinguished from individual initiation. Deep sedation, autonomic modulation and mechanical support as selected bridges with evidence and hemodynamic limitations.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; original VANISH primary trial 2016
checked: Ablation preferred over drug escalation after recurrent symptomatic monomorphic VT/shocks despite chronic amiodarone in coronary disease. VANISH prior-drug-failure population, escalation comparator and composite outcome 59.1 versus 68.5 percent; no isolated mortality inference.

sourceChecks.source: VANISH2 primary trial; multisociety ventricular ablation consensus 2019
checked: VANISH2 initial strategy, ischemic population, drug comparator and composite outcome; distinct from prior VANISH. Scar-channel reentry and substrate mapping when activation mapping is not tolerated; pace-map and noninducibility limitations.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmia guideline 2022 and ventricular ablation consensus 2019
checked: PVC burden around ten percent and higher risk above twenty percent interpreted as suspicion rather than proof; monitoring variability, CMR and response assessment. Ablation role in suspected PVC-induced cardiomyopathy distinguished from prophylactic treatment with preserved EF.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; multisociety ventricular ablation consensus 2019
checked: Outflow-type LBBB/inferior-axis morphology is a localization clue, with triggered and adenosine-sensitive mechanisms possible. ESC first-line ablation for symptomatic idiopathic RVOT/fascicular VT distinguished from other origins, observation and drug alternatives.

sourceChecks.source: Multisociety ventricular ablation consensus 2019; ESC cardiomyopathy guideline 2023
checked: Posterior fascicular RBBB/superior-axis pattern and specific verapamil-sensitive reentry, distinguished from undifferentiated WCT. Right ventricular arrhythmia red flags require integrated cardiomyopathy assessment despite normal screening echo.

sourceChecks.source: CAST primary mortality report; ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022
checked: Ectopy suppression does not establish survival benefit; class IC risk in post-MI scar. Exercise-associated complex symptomatic ventricular arrhythmia requires contextual investigation rather than automatic idiopathic, coronary or CPVT assignment.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; GeneReviews LQTS overview
checked: Repeated QTc at least 480 ms or score above three; conditional 460–479-ms criterion with arrhythmic syncope, measurement and secondary-cause caveats. Common genotype/current/trigger associations are probabilistic, not diagnostic proof.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; EHRA practical drug compendium 2025
checked: Preferred nadolol/propranolol and adult reference dose ranges; genotype-directed mexiletine with LQT3 evidence caveats. Secondary-prevention ICD and selected LCSD roles remain complementary to syndrome-directed medication.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; multisociety genetic testing consensus 2022
checked: Type 1 morphology, at least one V1/V2 and high lead positions; 2 mm equals 0.2 mV, avoiding apparent source HTML unit error. Induced-pattern specificity and negative SCN5A limitations; clinical events drive ICD consideration.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; EHRA storm consensus 2024
checked: Brugada storm: fever treatment, selected isoproterenol, quinidine and specialist ablation roles; distinguish CPVT catecholamine hazard. CPVT adrenergic bidirectional/polymorphic phenotype with normal resting ECG/structure and calcium-handling basis.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; EHRA storm consensus 2024
checked: Flecainide add-on after highest tolerated beta blockade with persistent adrenergic arrhythmia; LCSD and ICD escalation with continued medical suppression; no routine programmed-stimulation risk-stratification role.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; early repolarization pattern consensus 2015
checked: Inferolateral J-point pattern separated from syndrome after unexplained PVT/VF and from automatic ICD indication. Short-QT 320–360-ms conditional arrhythmic-syncope framework distinguished from terminal QRS notching.

sourceChecks.source: ESC ventricular arrhythmias 2022; AHA/ACC/HFSA HF guideline 2022
checked: Secondary prevention after documented VF without a reversible cause distinguished from primary-prevention EF cut-offs and waiting intervals; expected meaningful survival and residual substrate assessment.

sourceChecks.source: AHA/ACC/HFSA HF 2022; US ACS guideline 2025
checked: EF/symptom criteria distinguished: <=35 percent NYHA II–III versus <=30 percent NYHA I, treatment and meaningful-survival requirements. Standard >=40-day post-MI and >=90-day postrevascularization pathway distinguished from secondary-prevention and pacing exceptions.

sourceChecks.source: IRIS primary trial; US ACS 2025 and HF 2022 guidelines
checked: Early ICD trials separate arrhythmic death reduction from absent overall survival benefit, without causal death-conversion inference. US nonischemic DCM EF/symptom/GDMT/survival criteria distinct from CRT QRS criteria and European recommendation strength.

sourceChecks.source: DANISH primary trial; ESC VA 2022 and cardiomyopathy 2023
checked: Original DANISH all-cause versus sudden-death outcomes and CRT background; nonsignificance is not equivalence. ESC DCM EF below fifty and two risk factors, with LMNA-specific distinction and pathogenic-variant caveats.

sourceChecks.source: ICD appropriate use criteria 2025; MADIT-RIT primary report
checked: Conventional standalone S-ICD lacks ATP/chronic pacing/CRT, distinct from newer extravascular/modular systems. Programming evidence population, delayed/high-rate therapy and need to preserve detection of known slower VT.

sourceChecks.source: EHRA storm consensus 2024; VEST primary randomized report
checked: Confirmed oversensing requires supervised tachytherapy suspension with external rescue and definitive device review. VEST intention-to-treat primary arrhythmic endpoint, adherence limits and distinction from secondary mortality signal.

sourceChecks.source: APHRS/HRS sudden unexplained death family consensus 2020
checked: First-degree screening after young unexplained death, postmortem material review, phenotype-directed testing and VUS limitations; selected three-to-five-year reassessment until at least forty-five.

sourceChecks.source: ESC 2022 SQTS; EHRA/ACNAP rare-arrhythmia consensus 2026; modified LQTS score
checked: Modified diagnostic-score components and exclusions; QTc <=360 ms plus qualifying context, separate <=320 ms consideration pathway under ESC 2022, secondary prevention after VF, uncertain asymptomatic quinidine, pediatric scope of the 2026 pharmacological advice.
sourceChecks.accessLimit: 2026 publisher full-page retrieval failed; relevant indexed publisher diagnostic and clinical-advice sections were available and checked. No full-article access claim.

changes: Question 3 no longer introduces undocumented precordial concordance into a distractor; absence of RS complexes is the actual supplied criterion.
Question 7 removes an explicit atypical-origin clue and replaces qualified investigation distractors with realistic investigation names.
Question 10 removes giveaway qualification from unsynchronized-shock option.
Question 16 gives the amiodarone distractor a plausible correct component (culprit withdrawal), leaving drug selection as the discriminating error. Full-text review completed for questions 9–16.
Question 20 replaces an explicitly unsupported-transfer distractor with premature ICD-therapy suspension before rhythm verification.

Question 22 replaces claims of permanent autonomic/device cure with plausible but delayed ablation/rhythm-treatment sequences; rationales explain why concurrent escalation is needed. Full-text review completed for questions 17–24.
Question 25 specifies that VANISH2 counted death throughout follow-up and arrhythmic endpoint events after fourteen days.

Question 26 replaces atrial/PVI distractors with competing ventricular mapping strategies: prolonged intolerable activation mapping and targeting an incidental PVC. Full-text review completed for questions 25–32.

Question 12 replaces unrelated AV-nodal drugs with competing ventricular antiarrhythmic loading, maintenance and combination regimens. Regimen distinctions checked against the AHA 2025 tachyarrhythmia algorithm. Full-text review completed for questions 33–44; coverage and distractor issues remain separately open.
Question 31 replaces digoxin/magnesium with closer calcium-channel-blocker and general VT antiarrhythmic alternatives; retains the confirmed-mechanism wording that distinguishes verapamil.
Question 35 now includes the complete modified LQTS diagnostic score and counting limitations.
Added dedicated short-QT question at position 45; former questions 45–56 are now 46–57. Read all former questions 45–56 in full before renumbering.
